title.narrative: Business and Employment Recovery Program - Subprogram 2

description.narrative: The program supports the Government of the Philippines in building a business environment that fosters sustainable, high-quality jobs, particularly in the aftermath of the coronavirus disease (COVID-19). Subprogram 2 focuses on bridging the gap between skills training and employment, ensuring that the workforce is well-equipped to meet evolving industry needs. By expanding active labor market programs and liberalizing the business and investment framework, the program aims to increase the share of private sector jobs among total employment, significantly above the pre-pandemic level. It also promotes inclusive growth by increasing women's participation in technical and vocational education, providing them with better employment prospects. The program further supports vulnerable youth not in employment, education, or training and workers at risk of losing their jobs by providing them life skills and technical training and connecting them to private sector opportunities. In doing so, it contributes to the country's long-term vision of inclusive and resilient economic growth, as outlined in AmBisyon Natin 2040.

Reform area: Active labor market programs expanded to meet post-pandemic employment needs
Outcome: Total of 5,000 workers, including displaced workers, trained through the SUNPh scheme and private sector-led training programs (average 2020-2021 baseline: 0)
Description: 2.1 The government:
(i) through NERS Task Force, implemented the NERS action plan, and submitted the NERS terminal report to the Office of the President;
(ii) enacted the TPB Act, establishing a permanent structure for an IAC to generate sustainable and better-quality jobs in medium- to long-term; and
(iii) approved the implementing rules and regulations for the TPB Act.

Reform area: Active labor market programs expanded to meet post-pandemic employment needs
Outcome: Total of 5,000 workers, including displaced workers, trained through the SUNPh scheme and private sector-led training programs (average 2020-2021 baseline: 0)
Description: 2.2 The government, through DOLE, enhanced employment facilitation services by:
(i) increasing the number of institutionalized PESOs from 575 in 2021 to 725 in 2023, and established barangay-based PESOs from 6,465 in 2021 to 9,214 in 2023;
(ii) providing annual capacity building training programs to 731 PESO staff (52.7% women) on skills registry since 2022;
(iii) expanding the JSP program from 52 LGUs in 2022 to 60 LGUs in 2024, with more than 55% women among the beneficiaries; and
(iv) expanding the employer engagement program with the private sector under the JSP program by increasing unique employers from 138 in 2021 to 217 in 2023 and the employers on Youth Employment Exchange from 45 in 2021 to 141 in 2023, continuing JSP digitalization.

Reform area: Active labor market programs expanded to meet post-pandemic employment needs
Outcome: Total of 5,000 workers, including displaced workers, trained through the SUNPh scheme and private sector-led training programs (average 2020-2021 baseline: 0)
Description: 2.3 The government, through the DOT, DTI, and DOLE,
(i) completed training for 671 workers (including 319 women) across five priority sectors under the first phase of the SUNPh scheme and utilized the evaluation report to design the second phase; and
(ii) completed training for 858 workers (including 604 women) under the SUNPh scheme-inspired private sector-led training programs.

Reform area: Active labor market programs expanded to meet post-pandemic employment needs
Outcome: Total of 5,000 workers, including displaced workers, trained through the SUNPh scheme and private sector-led training programs (average 2020-2021 baseline: 0)
Description: 2.4 The government, through DOLE,
(i) approved a 6-year (2023-2028) plan to expand the coverage of the FWP to medium-sized firms, through provision of technical assistance and advocacy for the implementation of workplace welfare services to support women, especially pregnant and/or lactating mothers, such as, but not limited to, provision of breastfeeding stations, childcare and childminding services, nutrition programs, and compliance to policies that advocate for gender, family and women worker concerns;
(ii) started implementation by covering 732 medium-sized firms in 2023 and increased the coverage to 851 medium-sized firms in 2024, across all regions in the Philippines; and
(iii) approved piloting of childcare assistance for women in medium-sized firms under the FWP.

Reform area: Post-pandemic business and investment framework liberalized to enable job-rich growth
Outcome: Investment-to-GDP ratio increased to 25% (average 2020-2021 baseline: 19.3%)
Description: The government, through ARTA and SEC, further integrated eSPARC with the PBH by:
(i) covering all corporation types and partnerships that can be registered via the PBH;
(ii) using all available payment channels on eSPARC; and
(iii) operationalizing eSECURE to strengthen credentialing and eKYC of stakeholders for improved consumer protection.

Reform area: Post-pandemic business and investment framework liberalized to enable job-rich growth
Outcome: Investment-to-GDP ratio increased to 25% (average 2020-2021 baseline: 19.3%)
Description: To enhance the demand for skilled labor, the government implemented three key amendments to three investment-related laws designed to attract foreign investments in various sectors that include:
(i) the preferential hiring of Filipino workers by foreign retailers under the amended Retail Trade Liberalization Act of 2021; and
(ii) the understudy or skills development program mandated under the amended Public Service Act of 2022 and Foreign Investments Act of 2022, which require a minimum of two Filipino workers to be trained for each foreign employee hired by foreign-owned firms.

Action 1: The government, through the FIRB, operationalized an enhanced application, registration, and monitoring portal with the investment promotion agencies to minimize the manual submission of documents and monitoring reports. Operationalization included pilot testing and user testing.
Action 2: To enhance the demand for skilled labor, the government implemented three key amendments to three investment-related laws designed to attract foreign investments in various sectors that include:
(i) the preferential hiring of Filipino workers by foreign retailers under the amended Retail Trade Liberalization Act of 2021; and
(ii) the understudy or skills development program mandated under the amended Public Service Act of 2022 and Foreign Investments Act of 2022, which require a minimum of two Filipino workers to be trained for each foreign employee hired by foreign-owned firms.
Action 3: The government, through the NIC,
(i) launched the National Innovation Agenda and Strategy Document to establish a 10-year vision, long-term goals, and identified 10 innovation priority areas; and
(ii) awarded innovation grants to 13 projects in 2022 and 25 projects in 2023.
Action 4: The government, through ARTA and SEC, further integrated eSPARC with the PBH by:
(i) covering all corporation types and partnerships that can be registered via the PBH;
(ii) using all available payment channels on eSPARC; and
(iii) operationalizing eSECURE to strengthen credentialing and eKYC of stakeholders for improved consumer protection.
